memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them in a ceremonially clean place outside the camp. They are to be kept by the Israelite community for use in the water of cleansing; it is for purification from sin. The man who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he too will be unclean till evening. This will be a lasting ordinance both for the Israelites and for the foreigners residing among them." — Num 19:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ashes of the heifer were carefully gathered and stored, kept ready for whenever they would be needed. Mixed with water, they became "the water of cleansing... for purification from sin." God provided an ongoing, available means of purity that His people could draw upon whenever defilement came.

There is grace in this readiness. God did not require a new sacrifice every single time someone needed cleansing. He provided a lasting resource, kept and ready, so that cleansing was always at hand. His people never had to wonder whether purity was available to them; the provision was there, waiting to be used.

We see God's thoughtful care in this. He knew His people would face defilement again and again in the course of ordinary life. Rather than leaving them stranded, He made cleansing accessible and enduring. And note again the wideness of His grace: this provision was for the foreigner too, not only the native-born. God's cleansing reached beyond the boundaries people might draw.

For us, the availability of cleansing is fuller still. We do not draw from stored ashes but from the ever-available grace of Christ. His one sacrifice provides cleansing that never runs out, always ready the moment we come to Him. "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness." We never have to wonder whether cleansing is available; in Christ, it always is. His mercy is a well that never runs dry, open to all who come, from every nation and background.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that God's cleansing is always available?
2. Do you draw on the cleansing of Christ regularly, or try to carry your guilt alone?
3. What does the inclusion of the foreigner reveal about God's welcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ cleansing is always ready and available to me. When I sin, help me to come quickly to You rather than carrying my guilt alone. Thank You that Your mercy is open to all who come. Amen.
